risks.title: VPS accepts tactical records without the configured unique key
risks.consequence: Records without identity cannot be deduplicated reliably and may inflate tactical collections.
compensatingControls: All four tactical source producers create their configured deterministic identity key
The API rejects the complete append transaction when any tactical row lacks a non-empty string key
The 422 response identifies the collection, required key and every invalid row index
Contract and four-collection regression tests verify atomic rejection and unchanged duplicate behavior
risks.target: Maintain fail-closed tactical identity validation before persistence and require a separately reviewed migration design for any legacy exception.
risks.closureEvidence: PR #212 adds pre-persistence validation for snapshotKey, resultKey, eventKey and effectKey. tools/test-api-required-tactical-identity.py verifies missing, blank, non-object and mixed batches across all four tactical collections, byte-for-byte non-mutation, no temporary files, valid append/dedupe behavior and non-tactical compatibility. The updated API compatibility contract verifies analysis remains at zero missing keys. Final CI evidence is recorded on the pull request; production deployment is not implied.

risks.title: VPS API has no explicit request-body size limit
risks.consequence: Oversized authenticated requests can consume memory, CPU, and storage.
compensatingControls: Flask MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH defaults to 8 MiB and accepts only a positive integer environment override
Oversized requests return a stable machine-readable HTTP 413 response before persistence
Regression tests verify rejected append and replace payloads leave existing collection bytes unchanged
The request-size regression runs in both the security workflow and the always-running aggregate quality gate
risks.target: Maintain the tested request-size boundary and require reviewed evidence for any operational limit increase.
risks.closureEvidence: PR #210 adds the configurable 8 MiB MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH boundary and tools/test-api-request-size-limit.py verifies default and invalid configuration, stable 413 JSON, authentication order, byte-for-byte non-mutation, successful follow-up requests, and clean temporary-file state. Final workflow evidence is recorded on the pull request; production deployment is not implied.

risks.title: VPS API CORS policy is broad
risks.consequence: Unexpected browser origins may attempt authenticated API access if a token is exposed to that origin.
compensatingControls: CORS permission headers are limited to the four reviewed SLF game origins by default
The validated environment override rejects wildcard, null, credentials, paths, queries and fragments
Only GET, POST and OPTIONS with Authorization and Content-Type request headers are advertised
No-Origin authenticated requests remain functional for Tampermonkey extension transport
risks.target: Maintain an explicit reviewed origin allowlist and require test evidence before adding an origin.
risks.closureEvidence: PR #214 replaces broad CORS(app) configuration with an explicit /api/* allowlist and validated SLF_API_CORS_ORIGINS override. tools/test-api-cors-policy.py verifies every default origin, denied unrelated origins, allowed and denied preflight, no-Origin transport, normalized override behavior, disabled credential headers and invalid configuration startup failure. The aggregate API compatibility test also verifies allowed, denied and no-Origin behavior. Final CI evidence is recorded on the pull request; production deployment is not implied.

risks.title: External jQuery userscript dependency is URL-versioned but not content-addressed
risks.consequence: A compromised external distribution path could change executed dependency bytes without a repository diff.
compensatingControls: The userscript header contains zero external @require directives
Every registered runtime module is scanned for executable jQuery and dollar-alias references
The exact generated metadata and userscript artifacts reject any @require directive or removed CDN URL
Exact browser E2E executes the candidate without an injected external library
risks.target: Maintain a dependency-free userscript runtime unless a separately reviewed content-addressed dependency model is introduced.
risks.closureEvidence: PR #216 removes the unused jQuery @require directive. The security boundary requires an empty external dependency list and scans every bundle-order module for jQuery or dollar-alias runtime references. The exact artifact boundary requires both generated artifacts to contain zero @require directives and no code.jquery.com reference. Final exact-artifact, browser, security, governance and release evidence is recorded on the pull request; production publication is not implied.

risks.title: Browser DOM XSS coverage is not yet sink-complete
risks.boundary: Untrusted page and API text to userscript UI
risks.consequence: An unsafe render path could execute or inject attacker-controlled markup in the SLF page context.
compensatingControls: Dynamic code execution sinks are prohibited
Browser E2E executes the exact artifact and fails on runtime exceptions
Security scan inventories innerHTML assignments
risks.target: Classify every innerHTML assignment and add malicious-string fixtures for all untrusted data paths.

risks.title: Component workflows are path-filtered and cannot safely be required individually
risks.consequence: A skipped path-filtered workflow can leave a required status context pending and block unrelated merges.
compensatingControls: All prerequisite quality workflows are integrated into main
The rollout manifest requires an always-running aggregate check before protection is enabled
Branch protection remains explicitly not enforced until the aggregate context is observed
risks.target: Create and observe the exact aggregate status context, then configure and verify branch protection with a disposable pull request.

risks.title: No independent reviewer is currently available for critical repository changes
risks.consequence: The same maintainer can author requirements, implementation, tests, and approval, increasing the chance that a shared mistaken assumption passes every internal check.
compensatingControls: Owner acceptance is recorded explicitly and never described as independent review
Exact artifact, contract, security, browser E2E, property, fuzz, mutation, reliability, and provenance gates are integrated
Critical unresolved assumptions must remain in the risk register with review dates
Production deployment and branch-protection changes require separate explicit owner actions
Failures and skipped checks cannot be silently reclassified as successful review
risks.target: Use an independent qualified reviewer when one becomes available and reassess whether approval requirements can be increased.
risks.acceptance: Repository owner explicitly accepted this single-maintainer risk on 2026-08-04.
